verdict.rationale: Svelte's docs say components are written in HTML, CSS and JavaScript/TypeScript, with a `<script>` block, a scoped `<style>` block, and state that is "just a number" updated like any variable (svelte-docs-4, -5, -11, -38). Community reports corroborate the low learning curve: a back-end developer found it the most accessible option, and others cite fewer abstractions and closeness to Vue (svelte-comm-7, -8, -12). However, Svelte does add its own concepts: runes ($state, $derived, $effect, $state.raw), custom template blocks like `{#if}`, and a JS superset one user says hurt IDE support (svelte-docs-6, -7, -26, svelte-comm-20). Missing for 10: freedom from framework-specific syntax (runes and template block syntax remain extra concepts), seamless standard-JS tooling support.
